paragraphs.text: Recognize images via a dedicated vision subagent with independently configurable model
# dsh-image-bridge

Read images through a **dedicated vision subagent** whose model is configured
independently of the m

h a **dedicated vision subagent** whose model is configured
independently of the main agent's model.

Many text-first models (and any route the LLM runtime declares as text-only)
cannot see pixels: the

runtime projects every image block to placeholder text
before the request leaves the process. This p

lugin gives such an agent a tool
that looks at the image for it.
## What it does

- Registers one model-facing tool, `recognize_image` by default.
- On a call it resolves the images

the model pointed at (file paths, image
attachment ids, or the most recent image already in the conv

ersation),
stores them through the Harness attachment service, and starts a child agent
under `ctx.s

ubagents`.
- The child runs on **its own** `provider`/`model` from this plugin's config —
never the

parent's — with the images plus the caller's question, and its
answer comes back as plain text for t

he main model to use.
- The child runs at `maxDepth: 1` (it cannot spawn further agents of its own),

runs
with `delivery: 'caller'` (no completion notice leaks into the main
conversation), and is alwa

ys disposed after one question.
- While enabled, a short system-prompt line tells the main model tha

t this tool
exists, so a model whose runtime strips images knows to route them here.
## Configuration

Set these in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` entry `vision-bridge`, or edit the
`*`-marked fields l
ive from the Settings UI.
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `provider` | (required) | Child model provider id, e.g. `openai`, `anthropic`, `deepseek`. |
| `mo

del` | (required) | Child vision model id on that provider, e.g. `gpt-4o-mini`, `qwen-vl-max`. |
| `

reasoningEffort`* | `''` | Child-route reasoning effort id; empty uses the model default. |
| `maxTo

kens`* | `4096` | Output cap per child call. |
| `subagentProvider` | `spawn` | Backend on `ctx.suba

gents`; `spawn` ships with dsh base. |
| `subagentLabel` | `vision` | Label prefix for each vision c

hild; the question summary is appended. |
| `labelQuestionChars` | `40` | Characters of the question

appended to the child label so panel rows stay distinguishable; `0` keeps the bare label. |
| `tool

Name` | `recognize_image` | Model-facing tool name. |
| `maxDepth` | `1` | Absolute delegation-depth
cap; a child of the main agent is depth 1, so `1` admits the vision child but denies it grandchildr

en. |
| `timeoutMs` | `180000` | Per-call timeout. |
| `systemPrompt`* | `''` | Replace the child's

built-in analyst instruction. |
| `guideline`* | `true` | Add the "call this tool for images" prompt

analyst instruction. |
| `guideline`* | `true` | Add the "call this tool for images" prompt line. |

The bundled `cordis.patch.yml` leaves `provider`/`model` **empty on purpose** —
you must fill them i

n with a route in your profile that accepts image input.
The plugin refuses to run until both are se

t, and reports a clear error if a
call is attempted while they are still empty. It also checks the c

onfigured
model's declared `inputModalities` before starting the child and fails early
with a clear

message if that route does not accept images, instead of silently
sending placeholder text to a text

hat route does not accept images, instead of silently
sending placeholder text to a text-only model.
## Tool arguments

- `question` (required) — what to answer from the image(s).
- `images` (optional) — image file paths

(absolute or workspace-relative) or
image attachment ids. Several images are compared in one call.

Omit it to
read the most recent image sent in the conversation.
## Installing

This package is published to npm as `dsh-image-bridge` and installed as a DSH
profile bundle:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

or through the DSH plugin hub / plugin manager by package name. It ships
plain JavaScript (`lib/inde
x.js`) and needs no build step.

Runtime packages (`@deepseek-ai/cordis`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`,
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent`) are

declared as
**peer dependencies** and supplied by the Harness installation at load time —
the profil

e's module resolver routes these bare specifiers to the packages
bundled inside the app, so this pac

kage ships with no `node_modules/` of its
own and stays tiny. Only the Harness needs to provide them

; install nothing
extra.
